patterns.recommendation: Avoid longing when RSI is extremely overbought (>=65) even with strong directional conviction; these often reverse.
Short setups with strong trend strength (ADX>=27) and clear downward directional control (DI->=37) show the best edge; prioritize these.

patterns.condition: LONG with ADX >= 25 and DI+ gap (DI+ minus DI-) >= 15
patterns.recommendation: Avoid longing even with good directional gaps; this setup has consistently poor outcomes regardless of ADX strength.
Shorts with oversold RSI below 40 and confirmed trend (ADX>=20) offer neutral edge; use additional confirmation before entering.
Do not long when MACD is extremely elevated (>2.5) despite positive sentiment; momentum extremes precede reversals.

patterns.condition: LONG with RSI 50-60 and DI+ >= 40 and ADX >= 25
patterns.recommendation: This balanced setup with mid-range RSI, strong uptrend indicators, and confirmed trend strength offers the most reliable long conditions.

strongest_long_setup: LONG when RSI is 50-62 (not overbought), DI+ >= 40, ADX >= 25, and DI+ gap >= 15; avoids overbought reversals while maintaining directional and trend confirmation.
strongest_short_setup: SHORT when RSI < 40, ADX >= 27, DI- >= 37, and DI- significantly exceeds DI+ (gap >= 15); this captures momentum-confirmed downtrends with 63% win rate.
summary: Long trades are systemically underperforming (23% win rate on the primary setup), driven by poor risk/reward when entering with extreme RSI readings above 65 or high MACD values. Shorts show a clear edge when trend strength (ADX) and directional control (DI-) are both confirmed, achieving 63% win rates. The brain should drastically reduce long frequency and only enter longs in the 50-62 RSI zone with strong directional confluence, while leaning heavily into shorts when both ADX >= 27 and DI- clearly dominates.
